domains.name: auxiliary_heating
domains.description: Auxiliary heating systems including neutral beam, electron cyclotron, ion cyclotron, and lower hybrid
domains.reason: Names the heating actuators and their hardware.
domains.scope: The external systems that heat a plasma and their launch and coupling quantities, judged by whether the quantity belongs to a heating actuator or to the power it delivers. The heating method may be beams or waves; what decides the domain is that the quantity is about the injected power, not the transport it later causes.
includes: neutral-beam injection quantities — beam power, energy, current drive by injection — `nbi/*`
electron, ion cyclotron and lower-hybrid launch quantities — `ec_launchers/*`, `ic_antennas/*`,     `lh_antennas/*`
antenna and launcher hardware, and the coupling of power to the plasma
absorbed and launched heating power, and the heating system's efficiency

excludes.quantity: a wave field propagating in the plasma as such
excludes.rule: The antenna and the power it delivers are auxiliary_heating; the wave it launches, its dispersion and its wave-particle interaction inside the plasma are waves.

excludes.quantity: a non-inductive current driven by the heating
excludes.rule: The deposition of heat is auxiliary_heating; the driven current and its efficiency and control are current_drive.

excludes.quantity: a plant component that supplies the heating system
excludes.rule: A supply or cooling element serving an antenna is a plant component, plant_systems; the antenna and its launched power are auxiliary_heating.

domains.name: core_plasma_physics
domains.description: Core plasma profiles, kinetic quantities, global parameters, integrated quantities
domains.reason: Names the core plasma state, narrowed to quantities that are not a transport coefficient, a source or a profile form.
domains.scope: What a plasma is in its core: the values of its particle and energy distributions, the profiles built from them, and the global scalars integrated from those profiles, whether measured or modelled. Judge by whether the quantity is a state of the plasma rather than a rate of change, a diagnostic response or a data product.
includes: electron and ion temperature, density and pressure profiles — `core_profiles/profiles_1d/electrons/temperature`
toroidal and poloidal rotation and current-density profiles
composition, impurity and effective-charge profiles
moments of the distribution function — density, mean velocity, pressure tensor
global scalars integrated from the profiles — stored energy, plasma current, line-averaged density

excludes.quantity: a charge-exchange channel's ion concentration and charge state
excludes.rule: A charge-exchange channel's ion concentration and charge state are spectroscopy; the charge_exchange IDS is a spectroscopic diagnostic.

excludes.quantity: an interferometer's electron line density
excludes.rule: An interferometer's electron line density is electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics; the interferometer IDS is the wave-probe family.

excludes.quantity: power radiated, taken as an integral over the plasma
excludes.rule: Power radiated as an integral over the plasma is radiation_measurement_diagnostics; a bolometer's own quantity is the family's, not core_plasma_physics.

excludes.quantity: a transport coefficient, flux or source term
excludes.rule: How the plasma moves energy or particles is transport; the state it is in is core_plasma_physics. A profile's gradient is core; the flux that gradient drives is transport.

excludes.quantity: a raw diagnostic measurement that infers a profile, such as a Thomson scattering spectrum or a line-integrated chord
excludes.rule: The instrument response and its calibrated signal are a diagnostic domain; the profile derived from it is core_plasma_physics.

excludes.quantity: a geometry definition or a data-product wrapper
excludes.rule: A core-plasma quantity is core_plasma_physics even when its IDS is named like a profile container or carries solver numerics; the domain follows the subject of the quantity, never the folder it is filed under.

domains.name: current_drive
domains.description: Non-inductive current drive physics, efficiency, and profile control
domains.reason: Names non-inductive current generation, a physics distinct from the heating that accompanies it; its ten names are current-drive quantities, not heating-system ones.
domains.scope: The physics and profiles of current driven in the plasma by non-inductive means and the control of the current profile. Judge by whether the quantity states an amount of driven current, its efficiency, or the target current profile, rather than the power that drove it.
includes: driven current density and its profiles — `nbi/*/current_drive`, `ec_launchers/*/current_drive`
current-drive efficiency and the figure of merit for a drive method
the target and achieved current profile and its control
bootstrap and other self-generated current fractions

excludes.quantity: the injected power or deposition of the heating system
excludes.rule: The energy that was launched is auxiliary_heating; the current it drove is current_drive. Both may come from one beam, and the quantity's subject decides.

excludes.quantity: the total plasma current as a global plasma parameter
excludes.rule: The total current the plasma carries is a global state of the plasma, core_plasma_physics; the part of it driven externally and its efficiency are current_drive.

excludes.quantity: an ohmic-field loop voltage from the central solenoid
excludes.rule: The transformer that induces the current is a machine system; the current it drives in the plasma is current_drive.

domains.name: data_management
domains.description: Reference and auxiliary data, atomic and molecular data, summary data products, and computational and workflow infrastructure
domains.reason: Merged into data_management: its IDSs are reference or auxiliary data, atomic and molecular data, and computational infrastructure, not an area of physics. No live standard name carries it; its 1,959 live DD paths move with the vocabulary entry. Absorbs computational_workflow: both are non-physics data domains, and a reference-data IDS and a workflow IDS belong in one place. No live standard name carries either today; 1,959 live DD paths carry computational_workflow.
domains.scope: The dataset as such rather than the physics it records: dataset description, provenance, FAIR metadata and the archives kept for downstream use. Judge by whether the quantity says something about a dataset — what it contains, where it came from, when it was written — rather than about the plasma. A quantity that names a physical quantity takes that quantity's domain even when it is stored under a container such as `summary`, because the container records where the value is filed and not what it measures. It also holds the reference and auxiliary data, atomic and molecular data and computational infrastructure that computational_workflow named, merged here so one data domain carries them.
includes: dataset description, provenance and FAIR metadata — `dataset_description/*`, `dataset_fair/*`
archives, catalogues and manifests of a dataset
records of what a dataset holds, when it was produced and by what
atomic and molecular data services — `amns_data/*`
geometry definitions and computational geometry — `geometry/*`
generic and temporary containers — `temporary/*`
solver numerics and workflow tooling that carry no physics subject

excludes.quantity: a line-density constraint on the equilibrium
excludes.rule: A measured or reconstructed line-density constraint on the equilibrium is equilibrium; it is an equilibrium constraint, not a wave diagnostic or an assembled data product.

excludes.quantity: a directly measured or modelled plasma state
excludes.rule: A plasma profile is core_plasma_physics, and a summary quantity takes the domain of the physical quantity it names: an elongation under `summary` is equilibrium, a fusion neutron rate is neutronics, a plasma composition is the composition's domain. `data_management` holds only data about the dataset itself, and being summarised into a product does not turn a plasma quantity into such data.

excludes.quantity: operational metadata about a shot
excludes.rule: Operational metadata about how a shot ran is machine_operations; the archived data products from it are data_management.

excludes.quantity: atomic or molecular reference data
excludes.rule: A data product from a run is data_management; external atomic and molecular reference data is computational_workflow.

excludes.quantity: a passive loop element's own geometry
excludes.rule: A passive loop element's geometry is magnetic_field_systems; it is a machine component, not a computational geometry definition.

excludes.quantity: a barometry gauge's position
excludes.rule: A barometry gauge's position is mechanical_measurement_diagnostics; computational_workflow owns geometry definitions and tooling, not instrument hardware.

excludes.quantity: a physics quantity that a numeric or profile container happens to hold
excludes.rule: A physics quantity is its own domain even when it is stored in a solver-numerics or temporary container. The failing case this file exists to separate: a kinetic profile or a fast-particle distribution must not fall to computational_workflow merely because its IDS also carries numerics.

excludes.quantity: a physics quantity delivered as an assembled product
excludes.rule: Tooling and reference data are computational_workflow; a product that summarises physical quantities takes the domain of the quantities it names, never that of the container it is delivered in.

excludes.quantity: a structural geometry of a real component
excludes.rule: A computational geometry definition is computational_workflow; the structure of a real component is structural_components.

domains.name: distribution_quantities
domains.description: Distribution-function quantities: the distribution itself and its orbit-class moments
domains.reason: Added as a grouping of data structures: carries the distribution-function quantities section 6 divides out of transport, and owns the distributions IDS.
domains.scope: The distribution-function quantities a distributions structure holds: the distribution itself and its orbit-class moments.
includes: a distribution function or its moments
an orbit-class moment of a distribution

excludes.quantity: a fast-particle population summary
excludes.rule: A quantity read from the distributions structure is distribution_quantities; a name whose subject is the fast-particle population itself is fast_particles.

domains.name: divertor_physics
domains.description: Divertor target loads, detachment, particle and heat exhaust
domains.reason: Names divertor target loads, detachment and exhaust.
domains.scope: The divertor region's plasma and its exhaust of heat and particles: target loads, detachment, the radiation front and the ionisation and recombination in the divertor. Judge by whether the quantity concerns the divertor plasma rather than the edge globally or a wall surface.
includes: target heat and particle fluxes — `divertors/*`
detachment onset, the radiation front and its position
divertor plasma temperature, density and ionisation state
the divertor's neutral and impurity radiation

excludes.quantity: a general scrape-off-layer quantity away from the divertor target
excludes.rule: The edge plasma at large is edge_plasma_physics; the divertor's own target and exhaust physics is divertor_physics.

excludes.quantity: a wall-surface erosion or retention quantity
excludes.rule: The plasma arriving at the target is divertor_physics; the surface it erodes is plasma_wall_interactions.

excludes.quantity: an MHD instability during a disruption at the divertor
excludes.rule: The instability is magnetohydrodynamics; the plasma exhaust and target load that follow are divertor_physics.

domains.name: edge_plasma_physics
domains.description: Scrape-off layer, divertor physics, plasma-wall interactions, recycling
domains.reason: Names the boundary plasma, the most populous named area after transport.
domains.scope: The physics of the plasma outside the core and its boundary: the scrape-off layer, the pedestal, the edge transport barrier and the flows that carry plasma to the walls. Judge by whether the quantity describes plasma in the edge region rather than the core or a material surface.
includes: scrape-off-layer and edge profiles — `edge_profiles/*`
the edge transport barrier and pedestal structure and its height or width
radial electric field, edge flows and edge currents
the edge's own sources and sinks — `edge_sources/*`

excludes.quantity: a visible spectrometer's emissive channel
excludes.rule: A visible spectrometer's isotope density ratio and hot-neutral velocity are spectroscopy; the emissive channel is a spectroscopic diagnostic, whatever plasma region it observes.

excludes.quantity: a global loss-power scalar
excludes.rule: A global loss-power scalar is a core energy-balance quantity, so it is core_plasma_physics; a flux or diffusivity is transport, and an edge resolution is edge_plasma_physics.

excludes.quantity: a plasma-wall interaction on a material surface
excludes.rule: The edge plasma's behaviour near the wall is edge_plasma_physics; the surface's erosion, deposition or heat load and the material migration are plasma_wall_interactions.

excludes.quantity: a divertor target quantity
excludes.rule: Edge physics concerns the boundary plasma; target loads, detachment and the divertor's own heat and particle exhaust are divertor_physics.

excludes.quantity: the core plasma state
excludes.rule: A core profile is core_plasma_physics; the same quantity resolved in the scrape-off layer or pedestal region is edge_plasma_physics.

domains.name: electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics
domains.description: Interferometry, polarimetry, reflectometry, and wave-based diagnostics
domains.reason: Names interferometry, reflectometry and polarimetry.
domains.scope: Diagnostics that probe the plasma with electromagnetic waves and detect the wave's propagation: interferometry, polarimetry, reflectometry and refractometry. Judge by whether the instrument transmits a wave and measures its phase, polarisation or reflection.
includes: line-integrated density from interferometry — `interferometer/*`
Faraday-rotation and polarimetry measurements — `polarimeter/*`
reflectometry and refractometry profiles and fluctuation spectra — `reflectometer_profile/*`, `reflectometer_fluctuation/*`
the diagnostic's own frequencies, chords and calibration

excludes.quantity: a heating actuator's own launch geometry, such as an antenna module position
excludes.rule: An antenna module's mechanical position is auxiliary_heating; electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics owns a probe that transmits a wave and measures its phase, not the launcher's own hardware.

excludes.quantity: a line-density constraint on the equilibrium
excludes.rule: A measured or reconstructed line-density constraint on the equilibrium is equilibrium; it is an equilibrium constraint, not a wave diagnostic or an assembled data product.

excludes.quantity: electron cyclotron emission and the position correction of its channels
excludes.rule: Electron cyclotron emission is radiated power the plasma emits, so its position correction is radiation_measurement_diagnostics; a probe that transmits a wave is electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: a normalised flux coordinate along a ray path
excludes.rule: A normalised flux coordinate along a ray path is a flux-surface mapping, so it is equilibrium; a probe that transmits a wave is electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: an electron cyclotron emission channel position
excludes.rule: An ECE channel position is radiation_measurement_diagnostics; an ECE diagnostic records emitted cyclotron radiation rather than transmitting a probe wave.

excludes.quantity: a constraint on the equilibrium stored under equilibrium/time_slice/constraints
excludes.rule: A line-density constraint stored under equilibrium/time_slice/constraints is a constraint on the equilibrium; the interferometer that measured it is electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: a wave propagating in the plasma as physics
excludes.rule: A probe instrument and its measured signal are electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics; the plasma wave physics the probe studies is waves.

excludes.quantity: an emission line measured with a spectrometer
excludes.rule: Transmitting a wave to probe the plasma is electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics; passively measuring emitted light is spectroscopy.

excludes.quantity: a particle-counting measurement
excludes.rule: A wave probe is electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics; a measurement that counts particles or their scattering is particle_measurement_diagnostics.

domains.name: equilibrium
domains.description: MHD equilibrium, flux surfaces, magnetic geometry, coordinate systems
domains.reason: Names the force-balance configuration and its surfaces; the most settled group.
domains.scope: The static magnetic configuration of a plasma in force balance and the coordinate system it is expressed in: the flux-surface geometry, the poloidal flux and its radial derivatives, the safety factor, and the shape of the boundary. Judge by whether the quantity states where the field is and what shape its surfaces have, not by whether it is stored with a time coordinate.
includes: flux-surface geometry — boundary outline, major and minor radius, elongation, triangularity
poloidal flux and its radial derivative — `equilibrium/time_slice/profiles_1d/psi`, `psi_norm`
safety factor and magnetic shear along the profile
the equilibrium reconstruction itself — the currents and coils fitted to it
coordinate systems and the mapping between real space and flux space — `equilibrium/time_slice/profiles_1d/rho_tor`, `equilibrium/grids_ggd`

excludes.quantity: a ferritic field-shaping object
excludes.rule: A ferritic field-shaping object is magnetic_field_systems; equilibrium owns the field and its surfaces, and structural_components the load-bearing structure.

excludes.quantity: a fitted pedestal position
excludes.rule: A fitted pedestal position is a property of the pedestal region, so it is edge_plasma_physics; the flux-surface geometry it is expressed in stays equilibrium.

excludes.quantity: an electron cyclotron emission channel position
excludes.rule: An ECE channel position is radiation_measurement_diagnostics; the flux surface it is expressed against is equilibrium.

excludes.quantity: a heat, particle or momentum flux, a diffusivity or a confinement time
excludes.rule: A quantity that says how fast the plasma redistributes energy or particles — a flux, a diffusion coefficient, a confinement time — is transport; equilibrium holds only the field's shape and the mapping to it, never a flow across it.

excludes.quantity: the numerical value of a kinetic profile at a surface, such as the classical electron temperature
excludes.rule: The amplitude of a temperature or density profile is a property of the plasma, so it is core_plasma_physics; equilibrium owns the surface on which that value sits, not the value.

excludes.quantity: a growing instability, its growth rate or its stability limit
excludes.rule: A mode that destabilises the configuration is magnetohydrodynamics; a property of the converged, static configuration is equilibrium.

domains.name: fast_particles
domains.description: Fast ion and electron distributions, energetic particles, slowing-down
domains.reason: Names non-thermal fast-ion and fast-electron populations.
domains.scope: Populations of particles far from the thermal bulk — their distribution functions, slowing-down, thermalisation, and the instabilities they drive. Judge by whether the quantity describes a suprathermal population's distribution or its interaction with the plasma.
includes: fast-ion and fast-electron distribution functions — `distributions/*`
slowing-down and thermalisation quantities
fast-particle sources and their deposition — `distribution_sources/*`
fast-particle-driven modes and their effect on the distribution

excludes.quantity: a data-product or solver-numerics wrapper around a distribution
excludes.rule: A distribution of fast particles is fast_particles even when its IDS also holds solver numerics or auxiliary data; the domain follows the subject of the quantity, never the container it is filed in.

excludes.quantity: a neutral-beam heating quantity
excludes.rule: The beam and the power it injects are auxiliary_heating; the suprathermal population it creates in the plasma is fast_particles.

excludes.quantity: a thermal plasma profile
excludes.rule: The bulk thermal population is core_plasma_physics; the small suprathermal tail is fast_particles.

domains.name: fueling
domains.description: Gas injection, pellet injection, shattered pellet injection, fueling systems
domains.reason: Names gas and pellet injection systems and the quantities they deliver.
domains.scope: The injection of particles into a plasma and the systems that deliver them: gas puffing, pellets and shattered-pellet injection, and the resulting transport of injected neutrals and their ionisation source. Judge by whether the quantity concerns the delivery or the source of particles rather than the plasma's own density.
includes: gas injection rates, valve and puff quantities — `gas_injection/*`
pellet quantities — velocity, mass, ablation rate — `pellets/*`
shattered-pellet injection quantities — `spi/*`
the ionisation source and density deposition from injected particles

excludes.quantity: the plasma's own density profile
excludes.rule: The delivered particles are fueling; the density the plasma holds as a result is core_plasma_physics.

excludes.quantity: a pumping or plant component
excludes.rule: The gas and pellet systems that inject are fueling; the pumping and gas-supply plant that supports them is plant_systems.

excludes.quantity: a particle source term for the transport equations
excludes.rule: The injection itself and its deposition source are fueling; the transport of the injected particles through the plasma is transport.

domains.name: general
domains.description: Universal plasma physics quantities appearing across multiple IDS
domains.reason: An explicit last resort for quantities that cross domains, so no name is ever left without a domain.
domains.scope: Quantities that genuinely appear across many domains or carry no single physics subject, so no narrower domain fits. Hold this back: it is a last resort, and a path whose subject is knowable belongs in that subject's domain.
includes: universal quantities that recur identically across many domains and have no single subject
structural or placeholder quantities whose subject cannot be established

excludes.quantity: a quantity whose subject is knowable
excludes.rule: Choose the subject's own domain over general whenever the subject can be named; general is only for what remains after every narrower domain has been considered and rejected.

excludes.quantity: an auxiliary or tooling container
excludes.rule: Tooling and reference data are computational_workflow; general is for physical quantities with no single subject.

excludes.quantity: a summary data product
excludes.rule: A summary product takes the domain of the physical quantity it names; general is for a quantity with no single subject, and a container around many quantities does not supply one. A product about the dataset itself is data_management.

domains.name: gyrokinetics
domains.description: Gyrokinetic theory, simulation, and turbulence modeling
domains.reason: Names a model framework whose quantities describe the model world, not the measured machine.
domains.scope: The gyrokinetic model's own quantities: gyrocenter moments, the gyrokinetic distribution and its fluxes, expressed in the model's normalised coordinates. Judge by whether the quantity is defined within the gyrokinetic framework rather than in measured machine coordinates.
includes: gyrokinetic distribution and gyrocenter moments — `gyrokinetics/*`
normalised turbulent fluxes and their spectra in gyrokinetic coordinates — `gyrokinetics_local/*`
linear eigenmodes and their frequencies and growth rates
the gyrokinetic simulation's own input and output quantities

excludes.quantity: an edge-transport model's flux-limiter coordinate
excludes.rule: An edge-transport model's flux-limiter coordinate is transport; the model's own quantity in machine coordinates is not gyrokinetics, and a wall surface property is plasma_wall_interactions.

excludes.quantity: a broadband turbulence spectrum measured in the machine
excludes.rule: A quantity in the gyrokinetic model's own normalised coordinates is gyrokinetics; a fluctuation measured in the machine's coordinates is turbulence.

excludes.quantity: a coherent MHD mode and its growth rate
excludes.rule: A fluid-scale coherent instability is magnetohydrodynamics; a gyrokinetic eigenmode is gyrokinetics.

excludes.quantity: an experimental transport flux derived from a gyrokinetic model
excludes.rule: The model's internal flux is gyrokinetics; the mean transport flux it predicts or that is measured in the plasma is transport.

domains.name: machine_operations
domains.description: Pulse scheduling, workflow management, operational metadata
domains.reason: Names pulse scheduling and operational quantities.
domains.scope: The operation of the machine around a discharge: pulse scheduling, the shot cycle, workflow orchestration and operational metadata. Judge by whether the quantity concerns when and whether the machine runs rather than the physics it produces.
includes: pulse schedules and the shot cycle — `pulse_schedule/*`
workflow and orchestration metadata — `workflow/*`
operational configuration that is not physics — `real_time_data/*`
dataset description and fair-metadata records tied to an operation

excludes.quantity: a sensor attachment-point coordinate
excludes.rule: A sensor attachment-point coordinate is the mechanical state of a component, so it is mechanical_measurement_diagnostics; machine_operations owns scheduling, not hardware geometry.

excludes.quantity: a plasma-control reference during the discharge
excludes.rule: A command issued during the plasma is plasma_control; the schedule of when the shot runs and its phase is machine_operations.

excludes.quantity: a summary data product
excludes.rule: Operational metadata about a shot is machine_operations; the operation's own records do not become a data product by being summarised, and a summary of a physical quantity takes that quantity's domain instead.

excludes.quantity: a plant-system state
excludes.rule: The operational schedule of a shot is machine_operations; the state of the plant that supports it is plant_systems.

domains.name: magnetic_field_diagnostics
domains.description: Magnetic diagnostics, flux loops, Rogowski coils, diamagnetic measurements
domains.reason: Names the magnetic sensor set and its responses.
domains.scope: Diagnostics of the magnetic field and flux: magnetic probes, flux loops, Rogowski coils and diamagnetic loops. Judge by whether the instrument measures the magnetic field, its flux or the current it reveals.
includes: magnetic probe and Mirnov coil signals — `magnetics/*`
flux loops and the poloidal flux they measure
Rogowski coil and the current it measures
diamagnetic-loop and saddle-loop measurements

excludes.quantity: an MSE channel's detector geometry
excludes.rule: An MSE channel's detector geometry is spectroscopy; the motional Stark effect on the emitted light is a spectroscopic measurement, not neutronics or a magnetic sensor.

excludes.quantity: the equilibrium reconstructed from the measurements
excludes.rule: The coils' signals are magnetic_field_diagnostics; the flux-surface geometry reconstructed from them is equilibrium.

excludes.quantity: a coil or magnet as a machine system
excludes.rule: A sensing loop that measures the field is magnetic_field_diagnostics; a magnet or coil that generates the field is magnetic_field_systems.

excludes.quantity: an imaging or radiation measurement
excludes.rule: Measuring the magnetic field is magnetic_field_diagnostics; measuring emitted radiation is radiation_measurement_diagnostics.

domains.name: magnetic_field_systems
domains.description: Magnetic coil systems, superconducting magnets, field generation infrastructure
domains.reason: Names the coil and magnet infrastructure that generates the field.
domains.scope: The machines that generate and confine the magnetic field: coil systems, superconducting magnets and the iron or ferritic field-shaping infrastructure. Judge by whether the quantity describes the hardware that produces the field rather than the field it produces or measures.
includes: poloidal field coil systems and their currents — `pf_active/*`, `pf_passive/*`
toroidal field coils — `tf/*`
non-axisymmetric and error-field coils — `coils_non_axisymmetric/*`
iron core, ferritic and electromagnetic-coupling infrastructure — `iron_core/*`, `ferritic/*`, `em_coupling/*`

excludes.quantity: the magnetic field or flux reconstructed in the plasma
excludes.rule: The coils that make the field are magnetic_field_systems; the equilibrium field and its surfaces are equilibrium.

excludes.quantity: a measurement of the field
excludes.rule: A generator (a magnet or coil) is magnetic_field_systems; a sensor (a loop or probe) is magnetic_field_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: a control command that sets a coil current
excludes.rule: The coil hardware is magnetic_field_systems; the control command that sets its current is plasma_control.

domains.name: magnetohydrodynamics
domains.description: MHD stability, disruptions, instabilities, sawteeth, tearing modes
domains.reason: Names a distinct macroscopic instability physics.
domains.scope: The stability and macroscopic dynamics of a plasma as a conducting fluid: instabilities, their growth and saturation, magnetic reconnection and the events a loss of stability produces. Judge by whether the quantity describes a coherent mode, its mode numbers and growth, or the evolution of a disruption.
includes: linear and non-linear mode amplitudes, mode numbers, growth rates and mode frequencies
tearing, kink, ballooning and neoclassical tearing-mode quantities
disruption quantities — the thermal quench, current quench and their timing
sawtooth and other macroscopic relaxation events — `sawteeth/*`, `ntms/*`, `mhd/*`

excludes.quantity: a static property of the equilibrium the mode sits in
excludes.rule: The shape of the field is equilibrium; a mode that grows on it and its stability is magnetohydrodynamics.

excludes.quantity: a turbulent broadband fluctuation
excludes.rule: A single coherent mode with definite mode numbers is magnetohydrodynamics; a broadband turbulent spectrum is turbulence.

excludes.quantity: a plasma-control command that reacts to a stability event
excludes.rule: What the mode does is magnetohydrodynamics; what the controller commands in response is plasma_control.

domains.name: mechanical_measurement_diagnostics
domains.description: Mechanical and structural measurement diagnostics, strain, vibration
domains.reason: Names strain and vibration measurement.
domains.scope: Diagnostics of mechanical and structural quantities of machine components: strain, vibration, displacement and inertial or pressure measurement. Judge by whether the instrument measures the mechanical state of a component rather than the plasma or its fields.
includes: strain and stress gauges on machine components
vibration, acceleration and displacement measurement — `operational_instrumentation/*`
pressure and barometry measurement — `barometry/*`
structural monitoring instrumentation

excludes.quantity: a plasma parameter measurement
excludes.rule: A measurement of a machine component's mechanical state is mechanical_measurement_diagnostics; a measurement of a plasma parameter is plasma_measurement_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: the structural component itself
excludes.rule: The structure is structural_components; the instrument that measures its mechanical state is mechanical_measurement_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: a magnetic-field measurement
excludes.rule: Measuring strain or vibration is mechanical_measurement_diagnostics; measuring the magnetic field is magnetic_field_diagnostics.

domains.name: neutronics
domains.description: Neutron diagnostics, fusion product measurements, activation
domains.reason: Names neutron diagnostics and fusion-product measurement.
domains.scope: Neutron and fusion-product measurement and the activation they cause: neutron detection, fusion-product counting and the neutronics of the machine. Judge by whether the quantity concerns neutrons or fusion products and their interactions with materials.
includes: neutron diagnostics — `neutron_diagnostic/*`
fusion-product counting and the neutron emission rate
neutron activation and dose quantities
the neutron flux and spectrum at a measurement location

excludes.quantity: an MSE channel's detector geometry
excludes.rule: An MSE channel's detector geometry is spectroscopy (mse/*): the motional Stark effect on emitted light is a spectroscopic measurement, not neutronics or a magnetic sensor. Neutronics owns neutron detection and activation quantities.

excludes.quantity: an electromagnetic-radiation measurement
excludes.rule: Neutrons and fusion products are neutronics; photons, X-rays and imaging are radiation_measurement_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: the stored-energy or power balance of the plasma
excludes.rule: The plasma's energy state is core_plasma_physics; the neutron emission and its measurement are neutronics.

excludes.quantity: a structural component that is neutron-activated
excludes.rule: The component is structural_components; the neutronics of activation and dose in it is neutronics.

domains.name: particle_measurement_diagnostics
domains.description: Thomson scattering and particle-based diagnostic measurements
domains.reason: Names Thomson scattering, Langmuir probes and particle-based measurement.
domains.scope: Diagnostics that count or characterise particles to measure the plasma, chiefly Thomson scattering and other particle-based systems. Judge by whether the instrument works by scattering or collecting particles, rather than by an electromagnetic wave or the radiation the plasma emits.
includes: Thomson scattering spectra and the profiles they infer — `thomson_scattering/*`
Langmuir probe current-voltage characteristics — `langmuir_probes/*`
mass-spectrometer and neutral particle measurement
the diagnostic's own configuration — channels, geometry, calibration

excludes.quantity: a neutron detector's aperture geometry
excludes.rule: A neutron detector's aperture geometry is neutronics: the detector also counts particles, but the neutron-detection family determines its domain. Particle_measurement_diagnostics owns scattering or particle-counting instruments without a more specific family.

excludes.quantity: a barometry gauge's gas pressure
excludes.rule: A barometry gauge's gas pressure is mechanical_measurement_diagnostics; particle_measurement_diagnostics owns a scattering or particle-counting instrument.

excludes.quantity: a spectrum that measures emission rather than scattering
excludes.rule: A scattering or particle-collection measurement is particle_measurement_diagnostics; an emission spectrum analysed for species, temperature or field is spectroscopy.

excludes.quantity: a wave-based diagnostic such as interferometry or reflectometry
excludes.rule: Counting particles is particle_measurement_diagnostics; probing with electromagnetic waves and detecting their propagation is electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: the plasma profile derived from the measurement
excludes.rule: The instrument's raw and calibrated signals are the diagnostic domain; the physical profile reconstructed from them is core_plasma_physics.

domains.name: plant_systems
domains.description: Power supplies, cooling systems, vacuum systems, plant infrastructure
domains.reason: Names power, cooling and vacuum plant.
domains.scope: The auxiliaries and balance of plant that support a discharge without being plasma-facing or field-generating: power supplies, cooling, vacuum and gas handling. Judge by whether the quantity describes supporting infrastructure that acts on the machine as a whole.
includes: power-supply and electrical plant quantities
cooling-water and thermal plant quantities
vacuum pumping and gas-handling plant — `gas_pumping/*`
balance-of-plant monitoring — `balance_of_plant/*`

excludes.quantity: the pellet, gas or SPI system that injects into the plasma
excludes.rule: The injection system and its delivered particles are fueling; the gas handling, pumping and supply plant behind it is plant_systems.

excludes.quantity: a heating system's launcher or its power
excludes.rule: The launcher and its delivered power are auxiliary_heating; the power supply and cooling that serve it are plant_systems.

excludes.quantity: the field-generating coil system
excludes.rule: The coils are magnetic_field_systems; the plant that powers and cools them is plant_systems.

domains.name: plasma_control
domains.description: Plasma position and shape control, feedback systems, electromagnetic coupling
domains.reason: Names position and shape control and the feedback system.
domains.scope: The control of the plasma in real time: position and shape control, feedback loops and the reference and actuator signals that hold a discharge on its trajectory. Judge by whether the quantity is a control reference, a feedback signal or an actuator command rather than a plasma state.
includes: reference and target position, shape and current profiles — `control/*`, `controllers/*`
feedback loop quantities, gains and error signals
actuator commands for the poloidal field — `pf_active/*`
plasma-shape and position control during the discharge

excludes.quantity: the plasma state or equilibrium being controlled
excludes.rule: The commanded or reference configuration is plasma_control; the achieved equilibrium is equilibrium.

excludes.quantity: a machine system that generates the field
excludes.rule: The coil that generates the field is magnetic_field_systems; the control command that sets its current is plasma_control.

excludes.quantity: an MHD event the controller reacts to
excludes.rule: The mode is magnetohydrodynamics; the control response to it is plasma_control.

domains.name: plasma_initiation
domains.description: Plasma startup, breakdown, initiation physics, early heating phase
domains.reason: Names startup, breakdown and the early heating phase.
domains.scope: The start of a discharge: breakdown of the gas, the initial ionisation front, and the physics by which a burnthrough plasma is established. Judge by whether the quantity describes the very start of the plasma, before it is a confined, controlled discharge.
includes: breakdown and start-up quantities — `plasma_initiation/*`
the ionisation front position and speed
loop voltage and field-null configuration during breakdown
burnthrough and the early-current-rise phase

excludes.quantity: a plasma-control reference for the discharge that follows
excludes.rule: The breakdown itself is plasma_initiation; controlling the confined plasma that forms after it is plasma_control.

excludes.quantity: a magnetic-field-system definition
excludes.rule: The field-null configuration as a start-up physics quantity is plasma_initiation; the coils that produce it are magnetic_field_systems.

excludes.quantity: an operational schedule
excludes.rule: The physics of the breakdown is plasma_initiation; the schedule that triggers it is machine_operations.

domains.name: plasma_wall_interactions
domains.description: First wall, plasma-facing components, erosion, deposition, material migration
domains.reason: Names erosion, deposition and material migration at the wall.
domains.scope: The interaction between the plasma and the material surfaces it meets: erosion, deposition, material migration, fuel retention and the surface conditions that follow. Judge by whether the quantity is a property of a surface or of the interface rather than of the plasma volume.
includes: erosion and deposition rates and net erosion — `wall/*`
surface temperature, surface composition and material migration
fuel retention and recycling at the surface
first-wall and plasma-facing-component temperatures and fluxes

excludes.quantity: nuclear power deposited in a wall unit
excludes.rule: Nuclear power deposited in a wall unit is neutronics; the wall-surface erosion and retention that plasma_wall_interactions owns is a different quantity.

excludes.quantity: an edge-transport model's flux-limiter coordinate
excludes.rule: An edge-transport model's flux-limiter coordinate is transport; the model's own quantity in machine coordinates is not gyrokinetics, and a wall surface property is plasma_wall_interactions.

excludes.quantity: a disruption halo-current wall point
excludes.rule: A disruption halo-current wall point is part of the disruption evolution, so it is magnetohydrodynamics; plasma_wall_interactions owns the surface's erosion and retention.

excludes.quantity: an infrared camera's target-image coordinate
excludes.rule: An infrared camera's target-image coordinate is radiation_measurement_diagnostics; the wall surface's own response is plasma_wall_interactions.

excludes.quantity: the plasma's behaviour in the scrape-off layer
excludes.rule: The plasma near the wall is edge_plasma_physics; the wall surface's response to it is plasma_wall_interactions.

excludes.quantity: the structural or engineering definition of the wall component
excludes.rule: A component's material, geometry and support structure are structural_components; the erosion and deposition on its surface are plasma_wall_interactions.

excludes.quantity: a divertor plasma quantity such as the target heat flux in the plasma
excludes.rule: The plasma heat flux arriving at the target is divertor_physics; the target surface's erosion from it is plasma_wall_interactions.

domains.name: profile_quantities
domains.description: Profile quantities: the one- and two-dimensional profiles and their general-grid forms
domains.reason: Added as a grouping of data structures: carries the profile forms section 6 divides out of transport. It takes core_profiles and edge_profiles at IDS level because a profile IDS's content is this form, which leaves edge_plasma_physics with no IDS of its own — a question for the lead.
domains.scope: The profiles a profile structure holds: the one- and two-dimensional profile quantities and their general-grid forms.
includes: a quantity carried in profiles_1d or profiles_2d
a general-grid profile form

excludes.quantity: the transport coefficient that models the profile's flux
excludes.rule: A profile amplitude is profile_quantities; a modelled coefficient is transport_coefficients.

domains.name: radiation_measurement_diagnostics
domains.description: Bolometry, X-ray diagnostics, bremsstrahlung, imaging systems
domains.reason: Names bolometry, X-ray and imaging diagnostics.
domains.scope: Diagnostics of the radiation the plasma emits or of the imaging of it: bolometry, X-ray and bremsstrahlung detection, and the visible, IR and X-ray cameras. Judge by whether the instrument records radiated power, photon flux or an image, rather than a spectrum resolved in wavelength.
includes: radiated power from bolometry — `bolometer/*`
soft, hard X-ray and bremsstrahlung measurements — `soft_x_rays/*`, `hard_x_rays/*`, `bremsstrahlung_visible/*`
visible, infrared and X-ray camera images — `camera_visible/*`, `camera_ir/*`, `camera_x_rays/*`
imaging system configuration, sightlines and calibration

excludes.quantity: an emission spectrum analysed for species or temperature
excludes.rule: Recording radiated power, photon flux or an image is radiation_measurement_diagnostics; resolving an emission spectrum is spectroscopy. The failing case this file exists to separate: a spectrometer's line-of-sight emission belongs to spectroscopy, not to radiation_measurement_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: a magnetic measurement
excludes.rule: Measured photons or radiated power are radiation_measurement_diagnostics; measured magnetic flux or field is magnetic_field_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: neutron or fusion-product radiation
excludes.rule: Electromagnetic radiation (photons) is radiation_measurement_diagnostics; neutron and fusion-product measurement is neutronics.

domains.name: runaway_electrons
domains.description: Runaway electron physics, avalanche generation, loss mechanisms
domains.reason: Names avalanche generation and runaway loss physics, a distinct population with its own IDS.
domains.scope: The runaway electron population produced when the accelerating electric field exceeds collisional drag: its generation, avalanche growth, confinement and loss. Judge by whether the quantity is specific to a runaway population rather than a general fast electron.
includes: runaway electron density, current and energy distribution
primary generation and avalanche growth rates
runaway loss and wall-stability quantities
the runaway population's effect during disruptions — `runaway_electrons/*`

excludes.quantity: a general suprathermal fast-particle distribution
excludes.rule: A suprathermal population in general is fast_particles; the specific runaway population driven by the electric field is runaway_electrons.

excludes.quantity: the disruption that produced the runaways
excludes.rule: The disruption event is magnetohydrodynamics; the runaway population it generates is runaway_electrons.

excludes.quantity: a control action to mitigate the runaways
excludes.rule: The runaway population is runaway_electrons; the commanded mitigation and its feedback are plasma_control.

domains.name: source_quantities
domains.description: Source terms: the particle, energy, momentum and current rates a source adds to the plasma
domains.reason: Added as a grouping of data structures: carries the source terms section 6 divides out of transport, and owns the three sources IDS.
domains.scope: The source terms a sources structure holds: the particle, energy, momentum and current rates a source adds to the plasma.
includes: a particle, energy, momentum or current source rate from a sources structure

excludes.quantity: the transport of what the source adds
excludes.rule: The rate a source adds is source_quantities; the flux that carries it is transport.

domains.name: spectroscopy
domains.description: Emission spectroscopy, charge exchange, motional Stark effect, impurity diagnostics
domains.reason: Names emission, charge-exchange and Stark spectroscopy.
domains.scope: Passive emission spectroscopy and its analysis: the spectrum of light the plasma emits, resolved in wavelength and interpreted for species, temperature, flows or the motional Stark effect. Judge by whether the quantity is an emission spectrum or an analysis of one.
includes: visible, UV, X-ray-crystal and mass emission spectra — `spectrometer_visible/*`, `spectrometer_uv/*`, `spectrometer_x_ray_crystal/*`, `spectrometer_mass/*`
impurity line identification and intensity
charge-exchange spectroscopy — `charge_exchange/*`
motional Stark effect measurement of the field — `mse/*`

excludes.quantity: a broadband radiated-power or imaging measurement
excludes.rule: A spectrum resolved in wavelength is spectroscopy; a bolometric power or a camera image is radiation_measurement_diagnostics. The failing case this file exists to separate: a spectrometer's emission is spectroscopy even though a spectrometer measures radiation.

excludes.quantity: a scattering measurement that counts particles
excludes.rule: A passively measured emission spectrum is spectroscopy; a scattering or particle-counting measurement is particle_measurement_diagnostics.

excludes.quantity: a wave-transmission probe
excludes.rule: Measuring emitted light is spectroscopy; transmitting a wave to probe the plasma is electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics.

domains.name: structural_components
domains.description: Vacuum vessel, cryostat, structural support systems
domains.reason: Names the vessel and load-bearing structure.
domains.scope: The static engineering structure of the device: vacuum vessel, cryostat, supports and the structural definition of components — materials, geometry and load paths. Judge by whether the quantity describes a structure that holds the machine rather than the plasma physics around it.
includes: vacuum vessel and cryostat structures — `cryostat/*`
structural supports and their mechanical definitions
breeding-blanket structures and component geometry — `breeding_blanket/*`
component material and geometry definitions

excludes.quantity: a ferritic field-shaping object
excludes.rule: A ferritic field-shaping object is magnetic_field_systems; equilibrium owns the field and its surfaces, and structural_components the load-bearing structure.

excludes.quantity: an interaction of plasma with a surface
excludes.rule: The component structure is structural_components; the erosion, deposition or heat load on its surface is plasma_wall_interactions.

excludes.quantity: a field-generating magnet
excludes.rule: A magnetic coil system is magnetic_field_systems; the passive structure that supports it is structural_components.

excludes.quantity: a plant system that serves the structure
excludes.rule: The structure is structural_components; the supply, cooling or vacuum plant that serves it is plant_systems.

domains.name: summary_quantities
domains.description: Summary forms: local values at named locations and the volume-, line- and flux-surface-averaged or integrated forms of a profile quantity
domains.reason: Added as a grouping of data structures: carries the summary forms section 6 divides out of transport, and owns the summary IDS.
domains.scope: The summary forms a summary structure holds: local values at named locations and the volume-, line- and flux-surface-averaged or integrated form of a profile quantity.
includes: a local value at a named location in the proposal's summary structure
a volume-, line- or flux-surface-averaged or integrated form

excludes.quantity: the profile the summary form averages
excludes.rule: The averaged form read from the summary structure is summary_quantities; the profile it averages is profile_quantities.

domains.name: transport
domains.description: The transport quantities whose source data structure does not resolve to one part, which stay here by name and are enumerated
domains.reason: Divided per the lead's ruling: 950 names go to the five quantity-form parts, and the names the data-structure rule cannot place stay here, enumerated by name.
domains.scope: The rates and sources by which a plasma redistributes particles, energy and momentum, and the coefficients and model parameters that predict them. Judge by whether the quantity measures or models a transport rate, not by the IDS that happens to carry it — an equilibrium IDS with a diffusion model still holds transport quantities.
includes: particle, energy and momentum fluxes, including their decomposed parts and errors
diffusivities, conductivities and pinch velocities from neoclassical or anomalous models
source and sink terms for the transport equations — `core_sources/source/profiles_1d/*`
flux-surface-averaged transport and the transport solver's own parameters — `plasma_transport/*`
heat and particle confinement times

excludes.quantity: a source term for a suprathermal distribution
excludes.rule: A source term with a distribution source in the distribution_sources IDS is fast_particles; a flux or diffusivity is transport.

excludes.quantity: a global loss-power scalar
excludes.rule: A global loss-power scalar is a core energy-balance quantity, so it is core_plasma_physics; a flux or diffusivity is transport, and an edge resolution is edge_plasma_physics.

excludes.quantity: a static shape property of the magnetic field, such as the safety factor or the separatrix position
excludes.rule: If the quantity describes the configuration's geometry rather than a movement of particles or energy through it, it is equilibrium. A transport model that references the safety factor does not make that factor transport.

excludes.quantity: the value of a kinetic profile such as temperature or density
excludes.rule: The plasma's own profile value is core_plasma_physics; a flux or diffusivity derived from it is transport.

excludes.quantity: a turbulent fluctuation amplitude, spectrum or correlation length
excludes.rule: The fluctuating field and its spectrum are turbulence; the mean flux it produces crosses into transport.

domains.name: transport_coefficients
domains.description: Transport-model quantities: diffusivities, conductivities, convection velocities and damping rates
domains.reason: Added as a grouping of data structures: carries the transport-model quantities section 6 divides out of transport, and owns the three transport IDS, whose whole content is this quantity form.
domains.scope: The transport-model quantities a transport model structure holds: the diffusivities, conductivities, convection velocities and damping rates that predict a transport flux.
includes: a diffusion coefficient or diffusivity from a transport-model structure
a convection velocity or damping rate from a transport-model structure

excludes.quantity: the flux a coefficient predicts
excludes.rule: The coefficient is transport_coefficients; a flux whose source structure is not a transport model is transport.

domains.name: turbulence
domains.description: Turbulence physics, fluctuations, turbulent transport, correlation analysis
domains.reason: Names fluctuation and turbulent-transport physics, distinct from the transport rate it produces.
domains.scope: The fluctuating part of a plasma's fields and distributions: the amplitude, spectrum and correlation structure of turbulent fluctuations in density, temperature, potential and magnetic field. Judge by whether the quantity describes a fluctuation or its wavenumber-frequency spectrum rather than a mean value or a mean flux.
includes: fluctuation amplitudes and their spatial or wavenumber spectra — `turbulence/*`
correlation lengths and times, and cross-phase between fluctuating fields
radial and poloidal flux spectra of the turbulent fields
the turbulent-transport model inputs that describe the fluctuations themselves

excludes.quantity: a mean heat or particle flux produced by the turbulence
excludes.rule: The fluctuation and its spectrum are turbulence; once the quantity is the mean flux those fluctuations drive, it is transport — the essence of transport is the average, not the fluctuation.

excludes.quantity: a gyrokinetic simulation quantity from a gyrokinetics IDS
excludes.rule: A quantity expressed in the gyrokinetic model's own coordinates (gyrocenter moments, normalised fluxes) is gyrokinetics, even when it is turbulent in character.

excludes.quantity: an MHD mode amplitude or growth rate
excludes.rule: A coherent, macroscale unstable mode is magnetohydrodynamics; the broadband turbulent fluctuation is turbulence.

domains.name: waves
domains.description: Wave propagation, RF physics, wave-particle interactions, dispersion
domains.reason: Names wave propagation and wave-particle physics, separate from the heating systems that launch it.
domains.scope: Electromagnetic waves in a plasma: their propagation, dispersion, mode conversion, damping and wave-particle interaction, and the model quantities a wave code computes. Judge by whether the quantity describes a wave field or its interaction rather than the hardware that launched it.
includes: the wave electric and magnetic field and their polarisation — `waves/*`
dispersion relations, refractive index, ray trajectories and cut-offs/resonances
absorption, damping and mode-conversion coefficients
the wave's effect through quasilinear or wave-particle interaction terms

excludes.quantity: a normalised flux coordinate along a wave-code ray
excludes.rule: A normalised flux coordinate along a wave-code ray is both a flux-surface mapping and a quantity the wave code computes; precedence puts equilibrium first and settles the overlap.

excludes.quantity: a launcher, antenna or its delivered power
excludes.rule: Hardware and launched power are auxiliary_heating; the wave in the plasma and its propagation are waves.

excludes.quantity: a diagnostic that measures waves or the plasma
excludes.rule: A wave field inside the plasma is waves; an instrument that probes the plasma with waves and records a signal, such as interferometry, reflectometry or polarimetry, is a diagnostic.

excludes.quantity: an electrostatic fluctuation from turbulence
excludes.rule: A launched wave of definite frequency and mode is waves; a broadband turbulent fluctuation is turbulence.
